title: Jump: a central hub that warns the far side

trials.label: flash jumps to the right (and slightly up): left spot first, right spot 4 ticks later
the mirror, jump to the left (and slightly down): right spot first, left spot 4 ticks later

mechanism: The body has 50 cells: 46 ordinary cells and a 4-cell hub in the very middle, and both kinds sense light. An ordinary cell needs two ticks (steps of the clock) of light before it fires, so a flash on its own makes its spot fire one tick late, on a tick the scorer never reads. When the first flash (A) fires its cells, the hub passes the signal across the middle in one or two steps (one firing neighbour is enough to fire a hub cell; in trial 2, A's light falls on two hub cells and fires them directly), and every time a hub cell fires it gives the ordinary cells touching it a small nudge of charge. If the second flash (B) lands on a nudged cell, light plus nudge fires it on the very first tick, which is counted, so almost all counted firing (161 of 167 spikes in 96 trials) sits on the spot the flash jumped to. The nudge is short-lived: one hub spike keeps a cell ready for only about one tick, so in these 4-tick jumps it reaches B's cells either one tick before B's light (trial 2) or on the very same tick (trial 3); only the 4 cells that touch two hub cells get a double nudge that lasts long enough (up to 6 ticks) to answer when the flashes are 6-8 ticks apart. So it is a timing detector: the trip through the hub sets the delay, a cell fires early only when B's light and the nudge arrive together, and the same cells answer both flashes, with only their timing different.
evidence: Best of 15 jump runs: outputs/jump_f8/hex_sex_s1 (saved held-out score 0.80 on 48 trials). Fresh held-out trials: 0.81 on one 96-trial set, 0.73 averaged over ten 96-trial sets (0.68-0.76), 0.74 over twenty (0.68-0.81). The next-best organism (jump_evo s0) scores 0.55-0.57. With messages off it scores 0.00 and every trial is silent on the counted ticks. Counted spikes over 96 held-out trials: 0 before the flashes, 0 at A's first tick, 161 on B's spot at B's first tick, 6 anywhere else. Flash A alone or flash B alone gives 5 counted spikes each (scores 0.05 and -0.05), against 167 with both flashes. Hub tests: removing its 4 cells 0.00; turning them into ordinary cells 0.04; making every cell a hub 0.14; the exporter's 48-trial checks give 0.15 for shuffling where the two kinds sit and 0.10 for the best single kind. Making the hub blind to light: 0.76 to 0.73 at a 4-tick gap, 0.68 to 0.51 at a 3-tick gap (288 trials each). Cutting contacts (4-tick gap, 288 trials): hub-to-ordinary cut -0.01, ordinary-to-ordinary cut 0.73 (intact 0.76), hub-to-hub cut 0.19, so the hub alone carries the signal and does all the nudging. What fires B's ordinary cells on the counted tick (288 trials, an exact copy of the simulator that also records charge): at a 4-tick gap, the leftover nudge alone 242, a hub spike arriving that same tick alone 137, either one enough 87; at 3 ticks 12 / 279 / 47; at 6 and 8 ticks all 251 come from the leftover nudge, 244 of them from the 4 cells that touch two hub cells. Per-cell arithmetic: light adds 0.79 per tick against a firing level of 1; one hub spike adds 0.25, which keeps a lit cell ready for 1 tick; two add 0.5, ready for up to 6 ticks. Changing the gap between flashes (96 trials each): 1 tick -0.01, 2 ticks 0.05, 3 ticks 0.71, 4 ticks 0.81, 5-8 ticks 0.65-0.67, 10 ticks 0.19. Moving the jump's midpoint off-centre: within 1 site 0.73, within 2 sites 0.43, within 3 sites 0.20 (480 trials each). Hand-built 19-cell design from tests/test_task_jump.py, rebuilt on this lattice and run on the same twenty 96-trial sets: 0.64 (0.50-0.74) against 0.74, and the evolved organism wins all 20. The two share the ordinary cell's light sensitivity (3/8), fading (1/8 per tick) and rest after firing (3 ticks). They differ in the nudge (1/4 here, 3/8 hand-built, which lasts 4 ticks), in the relay cells (here they also sense light, with gain 1/2; hand-built relays are light-blind), and in layout (one central 4-cell hub here; 7 relays spread through the hand-built body).
